prompt: Production sprite atlas, 1536x1024, true transparent background, for Nostos, a painterly pixel-art 2D game inspired by ancient Greek Odyssey. Strict 2x2 grid of equal 768x512 cells, four isolated full figures with generous transparent gutters, no labels. The SAME mythological sea siren in all four cells: an adult Greek-looking woman with flowing dark hair, a modest dark blue-green woven chiton bodice and bronze clasp, with a long sinuous emerald-scaled fish tail, split translucent fin. The high overhead three-quarter camera (looking down 60 degrees) matches an action game viewed from above, and each figure faces RIGHT with the head on the right and tail on the left. All four poses are centered, comparable in size (roughly 550x300), identical design, clean coherent silhouette and subtle rich teal/gold palette. Top left swimming relaxed with tail sweeping slightly downward; top right swimming with tail sweeping slightly upward; bottom left twisting to look back, accelerating, with curved tail; bottom right a final distressed, tucked tail silhouette for when captured. Detailed painterly pixel-art (no vector or smooth illustration), dark outlines, sharp readable shapes at 85 pixels wide. Absolutely no water, no splash effects, no net, no scenery, no background lighting or shadows outside the silhouette, no text. Transparent alpha, game-ready.
alpha_cleanup_prompt: Edit this exact 1536x1024 sprite atlas. Preserve every original pose, position, line, color and 2x2 layout exactly. The only edit is remove the off-white background across the entire sheet and set it to genuine fully transparent alpha (alpha exactly 0 in the corners, spaces and margins; alpha opaque in sprite interiors with antialiased edges). Preserve pale blue fins and golden details. No white backdrop, white paper, fog, outlines around silhouettes, or checkerboard pixels; no rescaling, redraw or additions. Export true alpha RGBA. This is a background removal and clean silhouette extraction only.

scylla_entrance.prompt: Create a new cinematic background for the ending of the Sirens level of the same Greek Odyssey game. The first reference (open_deck) is the exact ship, deck design, camera, perspective and lighting reference. The second reference (cave_deck) is the geology and style reference for the next stage, which occurs INSIDE the cave. Generate the moment BEFORE entering it, the first view of the exterior sea entrance to Scylla's cave, seen from the ship's deck. Keep the ship composition very close to the first reference so the game can dissolve between them: aged wooden railing, narrow curved Greek prow at center, and mast and rigging on the far right. Beyond the railing, open dark teal sea leads to a tall rocky coast where a narrow natural mouth cuts between sheer basalt headlands slightly left of center. Show that the ship is approaching from open water with the open-air slate-blue sky and the coastal cliff tops visible above; do not depict the camera under a cave ceiling. A slim lane of softly moonlit sea and silver foam leads directly into that black passage. Storm is settling, low fog at water level, unnerving quiet and scale, cold slate and restrained teal contrasted by worn bronze and wood in foreground. Wide landscape art, painterly detailed pixel-art matching the references. Important focal point in the center-left upper half, with lower quarter allowed to be obscured by dialogue. No people, sirens, monsters, eyes, symbols, maps, interface or text. Authentic rocky shoreline rather than a constructed stone gate.
